intro: These words come from Yiddish daily newspapers printed in New York between 1910 and 1953 and held by the Library of Congress: Der Morgen Zshurnal, the Yidishes Tageblatt and Der Tog. Yiddish is written in Hebrew letters, right to left. Small marks on a letter count, so אַ and א are different letters here. The joined letter װ prints the same as two separate letters וו, so they count as the same and are never highlighted (likewise ײ and ױ). These pages were picked from ones our quality check rated as heavily damaged, so many are worn or badly printed.
name: Yiddish

notes.ב: the bottom line sticks out past the right side; כ is rounded with no tail
notes.ד: a sharp corner that sticks out at the top right; ר is rounded
notes.ה: the left leg doesn't touch the top bar; in ח it does
notes.ו: stops at the line; ן goes below it
notes.ח: the left leg joins the top bar; in ה there's a gap
notes.כ: rounded, with no tail at the bottom right; ב has one
notes.ם: square at the bottom; ס is round
notes.ן: a long stroke that goes below the line; ו stops at the line
notes.ס: round at the bottom; ם is square
notes.ר: rounded at the top right; ד has a sharp corner

title: Yiddish newspapers
